chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Kufi narrated to us, Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, from Abdul Azeem ibn Abdullah al-Hasani, who said: He narrated to me Ali ibn Muhammad al-Askari, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father al-Ridha (peace be upon him), from his father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him).

He said: It is disliked for a man to have intercourse on the first night of the month, and in its middle, and in its last, for whoever does so, the child will be born insane. Do you not see that the insane person most often has an epileptic attack on the first, middle, and last nights of the month?
And he (peace be upon him) said: Whoever marries when the moon is in the Scorpion, will not see the good result.
And he (peace be upon him) said: Whoever marries at the new moon (conjunction) of the month, let him expect a miscarriage.

key_terms.لِسِقْطِ الْوَلَدِ: For the miscarriage of the child

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended and disliked times for marital intercourse and marriage according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) links lunar phases to physiological and spiritual states, advising against intercourse on the first, middle, and last nights of the lunar month, as offspring may be prone to insanity, a phenomenon corroborated by the timing of epileptic seizures. Furthermore, he cautions against marrying when the moon is in the constellation of Scorpio or during the new moon (muhaq), associating these times with potential miscarriage or lack of marital harmony. This tradition reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of 'takhassus al-ayyam' (specialization of days), where celestial movements are believed to influence human health and destiny.
